raw_response:
I am getting older, so this year I will not do anything too risky. On my land, wheat and maize are still the steady way to keep grain coming, and cotton gives me some cash if the price is decent. I have only 7.7 mu, so every yuan counts. I will keep about 5 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, same as what has worked for me, and put the other 2.7 mu in cotton. The men around me mostly do it this way too. I have well water, so if the rain fails I can still save the crop, but pumping costs money, so I will not water more than needed.

For wheat, I will use a common local variety and put enough base fertilizer so the seedlings come up strong, then topdress once in spring if the leaves look pale. For maize after wheat, the turnaround is tight, so I will harvest wheat and plant maize quickly with light field prep, no wasting time. Cotton takes more hand work, but on a small patch my family can still manage it. I will not chase very high yield with too much fertilizer because I still need cash in hand. Better to do what I know, watch the field, and add a little more only if the crop shows it needs it.
